text:
maya: Quick smoke run across USE1 / USW2 / EUW1 for the new quantized T5 variant. Goal: compare edge-routing vs direct-pop assignment for p50/p95 and throughput. Ran ~13k synthetic requests (mixed seq lengths). Summary below.

zach: Nice, can you paste the p50/p95 numbers and any kernel notes?

maya: Sure — here's the condensed table from the run logs (seq len mix ~ avg 120, tails up to 1024):
```
Region | Route   | GPU  | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | qps
USE1   | edge    | H100 | 18       | 120      | 210
USE1   | direct  | H100 | 14       | 95       | 260
USW2   | edge    | A100 | 22       | 170      | 180
USW2   | direct  | A100 | 17       | 115      | 220
EUW1   | edge    | H100 | 35       | 420      | 120
EUW1   | direct  | H100 | 28       | 290      | 160
```
Note: p95 numbers are end-to-end observed at the API gateway, incl network.

li-wei: EU tail is unexpectedly high. I saw TLS renegotiation spikes and occasional fallback to fallback_kernel_v2 (slower attention path) in the EU pool logs. That explains the 100–200ms extra on some requests.

maya: Confirmed. Kernel selection trace: ~2% of requests in EUW1 hit fallback_kernel_v2 because sequence-length heuristics flipped when KV cache wasn't warm. Also observed that enabling KV warmup on repeated sessions reduced p95 by ~30% after ~200 reqs for that session.

anika: Ops question — can we try enabling prefix caching at the edge for EU traffic to see if it reduces those cold-starts without moving all traffic direct?

ops-bot: Deploy-bot: Started canary route change: 10% of EUW1 traffic is now prioritized to direct-pop EUW1-optimized pool (canary id: canary-1973). Will monitor p95 over next 30m.

ryan: Capacity sizing note from these numbers: to hit our SLA (p95 < 250ms) in EUW1 we should provision ~1.5x H100s based on observed qps headroom. A100 pools will need ~1.8x due to larger p95 variance. Planning: reserve headroom in Dedicated for EU until caching improvements land.

zach: Did you also compare quantization variants? INT8 vs FP16? Any quality regressions?

maya: Ran INT8 + qkv-packing config. Quality on our eval set: delta < 0.8% on our relevance metric. Small hallucination rate increase noticed in ~0.2% of logs — those are being triaged. Performance-wise INT8 gives ~20–25% throughput uplift and p50 benefit, but p95 still dominated by routing + kernel fallback.

li-wei: Next steps I propose: 1) 1h steady-state run with 95th-percentile seq length synthetic load, 2) enable prefix caching at edge for EU, 3) collect per-kernel hotpath traces and full stack traces for fallback events.

anika: I'll book the canary window tomorrow 09:00 PST and add the trace collection hooks. :thumbsup:

maya: Curl we used for the benchmark (headers matter — include routing header):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\
 -H "X-Redwood-Routing: edge" \\
 -d '{"model":"t5-quant-int8","prompt":"<sample>","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}'
```

ops-bot: Alert created (euw1-p95-tail): EUW1 p95 > 300ms for >5m -> paging on-call.

maya: Thanks — I'll attach the raw traces and the small eval set slice to the ticket once the canary finishes.

zach: Good plan. Also worth testing with TLS offload at edge proxy to rule out router-side crypto cost.

li-wei: Agreed. I'll add a quick A/B for TLS offload vs in-pop termination in the next run.

anika: Scheduling notes in the ops runbook updated (canary id canary-1973).

maya: Closing loop here after canary results come in — leaving this thread for follow-ups. :bar_chart:
